plan.step: Phase 2: Clarify - Parity and gate promotion

accepted_answers: Every promoted Bash-backed helper requires golden fixtures plus source-checkout Bash comparison.
Golden-only fixtures are limited to runner envelope/registry dispatch, typed-path/subprocess safety, malformed request, synthetic Windows/no-Bash/path, and normalization unit tests.
Normalization is allowlisted to volatile path, temp, timestamp, executable/version, platform/runtime identity, and live git metadata fields.

Promotion is recorded in a per-helper matrix with helper id, slice, Bash path, runner module/operation, fixture ids, comparison ids, normalized fields, status, authoritative test command, and deferred follow-up.
validate-pr-packet parity excludes validation-result and workflow-event persistence writes.

plan.step: Phase 2: Clarify - Parity and gate promotion Consensus

result.outcome: validate-pr-packet persistence remains out of scope; read-only validation output is in scope

plan.step: Phase 2: Clarify - Platform smoke and cutover boundary

accepted_answers: Smallest local macOS source-checkout smoke is a runtime-info JSON request through PYTHONPATH=speckit-pro python3 -m speckit_pro_runner.
The smoke proves source-checkout runner launch, JSON stdin envelope handling, one JSON stdout response, ok status, source_checkout context, and runtime/plugin-relative metadata.
The smoke does not prove installed-cache launch, generated payload propagation, active Claude/Codex invocation, helper parity, mutation-helper safety, or full native platform support.
The spec prevents cutover scope by limiting XPLAT-005 to source helper ports, tests, parity evidence, and internal review packets.
